Definition: Casluchim, a people cognate to the Egyptians
BiblicalUsage: The Casluchim are a people of the table of nations, sons of Mizraim, from whom the Philistines came. They appear only in the genealogies, a branch of Egypt's line whose descendants would become Israel's long enemies.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even a two-verse people has a place in God's record, because the nations all come from somewhere and His story runs through every one of them.
